prompt_v3_final:
A black-and-white children's coloring-book page, square 1:1, 1080x1080, drawn as an extreme close-up crop — like a photo taken so close to a big toy that the toy's own edges run straight off every side of the picture. The white paper of the page IS the picture; the linework itself is the only edge that exists.

SCENE: A cheerful ROBOT-LIKE RIBOSOME FACTORY MACHINE character is busy at work threading beads onto a string.
- The RIBOSOME CHARACTER is built from two round, chunky, snowman-stacked body parts: a HUGE round body, and a MUCH SMALLER round head-part sitting on top of it like a small pom-pom hat or a beach ball balanced on a boulder — the top part's diameter is only about HALF the width of the bottom part, obviously and dramatically smaller. Draw one big happy round face in the middle of the BOTTOM (bigger) part: two large round eyes with pupils, cheerful eyebrows and a wide open smile. Give the whole character a smooth, thick, even double outline (two closely-spaced smooth curved lines with a thin white gap between them, like a friendly padded robot suit).
- Draw the bottom body part SO LARGE that its own round outline runs past the left edge, the right edge AND the bottom edge of the picture all at once — pretend the picture was cropped in tight afterwards, so only the character's face and upper body are fully visible and the rest of its round body is simply cut off by the paper's edge, exactly the way a close-up photograph crops off whatever is too big to fit.
- Across the middle of the character, right where the small top part meets the big bottom part, draw a long WAVY RIBBON TAPE feeding in from the left picture edge (it enters already cut off by the edge) and threading straight through a simple horizontal slot in the character's body — a single plain wavy ribbon with no writing on it.
- Along the tape, inside the character, draw three simple round friendly BEAD-HOLDER hands or clips (small rounded mitten or clamp shapes) gripping the tape one after another, evenly spaced — plain rounded shapes, no letters or symbols on any of them.
- From the right side of the character, a long STRING OF ROUND BEADS (like a pearl necklace of big round candy beads) comes out through a separate round opening lower on the big bottom body part and loops playfully toward the right picture edge, running off the picture there, cut off by the edge. Draw the beads big, round, chunky and simple, a couple with a small friendly smiling face on them.
- In the upper-right corner, partly cut off by the top edge and the right edge, draw a SECOND smaller friendly ribosome-factory character (same snowman-stacked two-round-parts shape, top part clearly smaller than bottom part, one simple happy face) riding further along the SAME wavy tape, also threading its own shorter string of round beads.
- Fill any remaining open paper with a loose scatter of extra plain round beads and small plain circles of different sizes, several of them positioned right at the top, left, right and bottom edges so they too are cut off by the picture's border, leaving generous open white space inside every shape for a child to colour.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- Bold, thick, even black outlines on pure white paper. Every shape a simple closed line.
- No shading, no grey tones, no hatching, no stippling, no gradients, no colour fill, no solid black fill anywhere except small solid pupils in the eyes.
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of open white space for colouring.
- The picture fills the entire square canvas edge-to-edge on every side — every one of the four edges of the square has linework crossing it (the big body, the tape, the bead-string, the second character, or the background beads), so that no strip of empty paper margin runs along any edge.

Avoid: pointed rays, spikes, sparkle or starburst shapes of any kind; any rectangle, panel, ground-line, shelf or vignette drawn around the scene; any text, letters, numbers or captions; any speech bubble (added separately afterwards); a twisted double-helix ladder for the tape (it is a single flat ribbon); human hands or arrows; the two round body parts drawn the same size as each other.
